The framework integrates inference, control, and execution under endogenous uncertainty, modeling investment decisions as coupled dynamics of belief updating, preference encoding, and action selection rather than optimization over fixed objectives. In this approach, portfolio behavior is governed by the expected free energy (EFE) minimization, showing that classical valuation models emerge as limiting cases when epistemic components vanish. Using train-test evaluation on the ARKK Innovation ETF (2015-2025), we identify a Passivity Paradox: frozen belief transfer outperforms naive adaptive learning. A Professional Agent achieves a Sharpe ratio of 0.39 while its adaptive counterpart degrades to -0.28, reflecting belief contamination when learning from policy-dependent signals.
